references.text: The source and candidate 0 together form the complete account of Jacob receiving the name Israel; the source shows the question before the change, while candidate 0 shows the actual change.
Both verses show God's initiative to meet Jacob by name, where candidate 2 marks the start of a new phase (the dream) and the source marks the end of the old identity before the name change.
A clear contrast in Jacob's life: In candidate 5 he uses the name Esau to deceive his father, while in the source he must stand by his own name 'Jacob' before he can receive the new name Israel.
A strong theological contrast: Jacob receives a new, unified name from God (the source), while the possessed man has the name 'Legion', representing chaos and many (Mark 5:9).
